etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English symply, symplely; equivalent to simple +‎ -ly, with *-lely simplified to -ly by haplology.

definitions.definition: (manner) In a simple way or state; considered in or by itself; without addition; alone.

quote.citation: 1791, Charlotte Smith, Celestina, Broadview, published 2004, page 179:
quote.text: Mrs. Thorold had told her sons that a young lady was visiting at the house, whose history she had given them in short hand, describing her as a dependent on the late Mrs. Willoughby, whom her son had very simply intended to marry at Alvestone  […] .

quote.citation: 2013 June 1, “Ideas coming down the track”, in The Economist, volume 407, number 8838, page 13 (Technology Quarterly):
quote.text: A “moving platform” scheme […] is more technologically ambitious than maglev trains even though it relies on conventional rails. […] This set-up solves several problems […]. Stopping high-speed trains wastes energy and time, so why not simply slow them down enough for a moving platform to pull alongside?

quote.citation: 2019 May 21, Dylan Curran, “Facial recognition will soon be everywhere. Are we prepared?”, in The Guardian‎[1]:
quote.text: Rather than scanning a boarding pass or handing over a passport, you simply stare into a camera and you’re verified.
What about the way you love me? / And the way you squeeze me? / Simply beautiful
